key_insight: PathMem adds a cognition-aligned memory transformation layer to pathology MLLMs, enabling explicit integration of structured domain knowledge (taxonomy, grading criteria, clinical evidence) with visual features to produce more interpretable, criteria-linked diagnostic reasoning.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between powerful multimodal reasoning and the need for structured, interpretable knowledge integration in computational pathology—so MLLMs can link morphological evidence to formal diagnostic/grading criteria transparently.
method: Introduce a structured memory representation aligned to pathology concepts (taxonomy, grading rules, evidence items) that the MLLM can read/write.
Apply a memory transformation mechanism that fuses visual features from pathology images with domain knowledge units so that reasoning references specific criteria.
Provide interpretable memory traces and retrievals that expose which criteria and evidence contributed to a diagnosis.
impact: Makes pathology MLLMs clinically more usable by improving traceability and alignment with domain standards—helping practitioners trust, audit, and integrate AI outputs into diagnostic workflows.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: MLLM + PathMem module showing memory slots for taxonomy, criteria, and evidence and their interfaces with vision and language encoders.
Flowchart/example case: Slide image → extracted features → memory fusion → criteria-linked diagnosis with highlighted evidence.
Memory visualization: timeline or matrix showing memory slots, activated concepts, and interpretable traces used for a specific prediction.
Comparison chart: accuracy/interpretability trade-off vs. baseline MLLMs (e.g., improved explainability and criteria adherence).
paper_title: PathMem: Toward Cognition-Aligned Memory Transformation for Pathology MLLMs
paper_authors: Jinyue Li, Yuci Liang, Qiankun Li, Xinheng Lyu, Jiayu Qian
